title: New Pill Offers Hope for Pancreatic Cancer Patients
subtitle: Early trial results show a daily drug may help shrink tumours and extend survival for those with advanced disease.

summary.en: A new daily pill called daraxonrasib is being called a major breakthrough for treating pancreatic cancer. In a recent trial, the drug helped shrink or eliminate tumours in a majority of participants. Experts believe this treatment could change how doctors manage one of the deadliest forms of cancer. While the results are very encouraging, doctors warn that more research is needed to confirm if it is a long-term cure. The drug works by targeting specific gene mutations that cause cancer cells to grow.
summary.zh: 一種名為 daraxonrasib 的新型每日口服藥物，被譽為治療胰臟癌的重大突破。在近期的一項試驗中，該藥物幫助多數參與者的腫瘤縮小或消失。專家認為，這種療法可能改變醫師處理這種最致命癌症之一的方式。儘管結果非常令人振奮，醫師仍警告需要更多研究來證實其是否為長期治癒。該藥物的作用機制是鎖定導致癌細胞生長的特定基因突變。

paragraphs.en: Doctors and researchers are celebrating a new development in the fight against pancreatic cancer. A new daily pill, known as daraxonrasib, has shown promising results in early medical trials. Experts are calling it the most significant step forward in decades for a disease that is notoriously difficult to treat.
paragraphs.zh: 醫師與研究人員正為對抗胰臟癌的一項新進展慶祝。一種名為 daraxonrasib 的新型每日口服藥物，在早期的醫學試驗中展現了令人期待的成果。專家稱這是數十年來，針對這種以難以治療著稱的疾病，所邁出的最重要一步。

paragraphs.en: Pancreatic cancer is often called one of the deadliest forms of the disease. According to The Guardian, it has the lowest survival rate of all common cancers in the UK, and patients often face a very poor outlook. Currently, most people diagnosed with advanced pancreatic cancer do not live long, and standard chemotherapy often fails to stop the cancer from growing again. Because of this, medical professionals have long searched for better ways to help patients.
paragraphs.zh: 胰臟癌常被稱為最致命的癌症類型之一。根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，它是英國所有常見癌症中存活率最低的，患者通常面臨極差的預後。目前，大多數被診斷出晚期胰臟癌的患者壽命並不長，且標準化學治療往往無法阻止癌症復發。正因如此，醫療專業人員長期以來一直在尋找能幫助患者的更好方法。

paragraphs.en: In a recent study involving 61 participants, researchers tested daraxonrasib alongside chemotherapy. The results were highly encouraging. According to the BBC, tumours stopped growing in almost all of the patients involved in the study. Furthermore, just over 60% of participants saw their tumours shrink or disappear entirely. In about 8% of cases—or one in 12 patients—the cancer became undetectable on CT scans. Dr. Wungki Park, who presented these findings at a medical conference in Barcelona, described the results as the closest thing to a cure he has ever seen for patients whose cancer had already spread to other parts of the body.
paragraphs.zh: 在一項涉及 61 名參與者的近期研究中，研究人員測試了 daraxonrasib 搭配化學治療的效果。結果相當令人振奮。根據 BBC 報導，幾乎所有參與研究的患者，其腫瘤都停止生長。此外，超過 60% 的參與者腫瘤縮小或完全消失。在大約 8% 的病例中，也就是每 12 名患者中就有 1 人，癌症在電腦斷層掃描中已無法偵測到。在巴塞隆納一場醫學會議上發表這些發現的朴永基醫師（Dr. Wungki Park）形容，對於癌症已經擴散到身體其他部位的患者來說，這是他見過最接近治癒的成果。

paragraphs.en: So, how does this new treatment work? Daraxonrasib is a targeted inhibitor. This means it is designed to lock onto and shut off specific gene mutations, known as RAS, which drive the growth of most pancreatic cancer cells. By stopping these mutations, the drug prevents the cancer from spreading as quickly. MedPage Today reports that this approach could be "transformative" for patients, as it moves beyond traditional chemotherapy to attack the root cause of the tumour growth.
paragraphs.zh: 那麼，這種新療法是如何運作的呢？Daraxonrasib 是一種標靶抑制劑。這意味著它旨在鎖定並關閉特定的基因突變，即所謂的 RAS，這些突變是驅動大多數胰臟癌細胞生長的主因。透過阻斷這些突變，該藥物能防止癌症快速擴散。《今日醫學網》（MedPage Today）報導指出，這種方法對患者而言可能是「革命性」的，因為它超越了傳統化學治療，直接攻擊腫瘤生長的根本原因。

paragraphs.en: Despite the excitement, medical experts are urging caution. While the results are impressive, doctors emphasize that it is too early to call this pill a permanent cure. It remains unclear exactly how long the drug can keep the disease under control. Dr. Sam Godfrey of Cancer Research UK noted that while the progress is long overdue, more time and larger studies are necessary to understand if the cancer will return. He explained that even if a scan shows no sign of cancer, patients cannot be certain they are fully free of the disease until more time has passed.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管各界感到興奮，醫學專家仍呼籲保持謹慎。雖然結果令人印象深刻，但醫師強調，現在稱這種藥丸為永久治癒還言之過早。目前尚不清楚該藥物究竟能將疾病控制多久。英國癌症研究協會（Cancer Research UK）的薩姆·戈弗雷醫師（Dr. Sam Godfrey）指出，雖然這項進展遲來已久，但仍需要更多時間與更大規模的研究，才能了解癌症是否會復發。他解釋說，即使掃描顯示沒有癌症跡象，在經過更長的時間之前，患者仍無法確定自己已完全擺脫疾病。

paragraphs.en: Looking ahead, there is hope that this treatment could benefit more than just pancreatic cancer patients. Because many other types of cancer—such as lung and ovarian cancer—share similar gene mutations, researchers believe the drug might eventually be used to treat a wide range of patients. Michelle Mitchell, the chief executive of Cancer Research UK, stated that this breakthrough could offer real hope to people facing some of the most difficult-to-treat cancers in the world.
paragraphs.zh: 展望未來，人們希望這種療法不僅能造福胰臟癌患者。由於許多其他類型的癌症，例如肺癌與卵巢癌，都具有相似的基因突變，研究人員相信該藥物最終可能用於治療廣泛的患者群體。英國癌症研究協會執行長蜜雪兒·米切爾（Michelle Mitchell）表示，這項突破能為那些面對全球最難治療癌症的患者，提供真正的希望。

paragraphs.en: Currently, the drug has already received approval in the United States for certain patients who have already tried other therapies. However, more research is required before it can be widely used in other healthcare systems, such as the NHS in the UK. Researchers are now planning longer, larger studies to confirm these initial findings. If these future trials are successful, it could mark a major change in how doctors treat advanced cancer, potentially giving patients more time with their families and a better quality of life.
paragraphs.zh: 目前，該藥物已在美國獲得批准，適用於部分已嘗試過其他療法的患者。然而，在廣泛應用於其他醫療體系（例如英國的國民保健署）之前，仍需進行更多研究。研究人員目前正計畫進行更長、更大規模的試驗，以證實這些初步發現。如果這些未來的試驗成功，將可能標誌著醫師治療晚期癌症方式的重大變革，並有望讓患者擁有更多與家人相處的時間，以及更好的生活品質。

keyTerms.definitionEn: The likely future situation or prospect for someone.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「觀點」或「人生觀」，這裡指病情的預後。文中：patients often face a very poor outlook.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To attach or fix firmly to something.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意為「鎖上」，這裡指藥物分子與基因突變結合。文中：This means it is designed to lock onto and shut off specific gene mutations, known as RAS, which drive the growth of most pancreatic cancer cells.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To cause or influence something to happen or develop.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作「駕駛」，這裡指導致癌症生長。文中：which drive the growth of most pancreatic cancer cells.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Happening later than expected or needed.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見於帳單或圖書館書籍「逾期」，這裡指醫學進展遲遲未到。文中：Dr. Sam Godfrey of Cancer Research UK noted that while the progress is long overdue, more time and larger studies are necessary to understand if the cancer will return.

quiz.question: What specific outcome was observed in approximately 8% of the study participants?

options.A: Their tumours began to grow again after initial chemotherapy.
options.B: The cancer was no longer visible on CT scan imaging.
options.C: They experienced a complete cure with no risk of recurrence.
options.D: The drug failed to interact with the RAS gene mutations.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 B。根據文章第三段，研究中約有 8% 的患者（即 12 分之 1）在 CT 掃描中無法再檢測到癌細胞。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到腫瘤停止生長而非再次生長。選項 C 錯誤，因為醫生強調目前尚無法斷定這是永久治癒。選項 D 錯誤，因為該藥物的機制正是針對 RAS 基因突變。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why are medical experts still hesitant to label daraxonrasib a 'cure'?

options.A: It has not yet been approved by any regulatory body in the world.
options.B: It only works on patients who have never received chemotherapy before.
options.C: There is insufficient long-term data to ensure the cancer will not return.
options.D: The drug has been shown to cause severe side effects in most participants.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 C。根據第五段，專家強調雖然結果令人印象深刻，但仍需更多時間與大規模研究，才能確認癌症是否會復發，因此現在稱其為「治癒」還言之過早。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到該藥物已在美國獲得批准。選項 B 錯誤，文章並未限制僅限於未接受過化療的患者。選項 D 錯誤，文中並未討論該藥物的副作用。

quiz.question: In the fourth paragraph, what does the word 'transformative' most closely mean as it is used in the context of the new treatment?

options.A: Having a significant and positive impact on the way something is done.
options.B: Physically changing the shape of the tumour cells.
options.C: Moving a patient from one hospital to another for better care.
options.D: Replacing old medical equipment with newer, more expensive technology.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 A。在第四段中，作者使用 'transformative' 來描述這種新療法如何超越傳統化療，從根本上攻擊腫瘤生長，意指其具有「變革性的」或「具有重大影響的」效果。選項 B 是字面上的誤解，並非指物理形狀改變。選項 C 與 D 皆與醫療流程或設備無關，不符合文中探討治療方法的語境。

quiz.question: What is the primary message of the article regarding daraxonrasib?

options.A: It is a proven, permanent cure for all types of cancer that will replace chemotherapy.
options.B: It is a promising new treatment for pancreatic cancer that requires further study.
options.C: It is a drug that only works for patients with lung and ovarian cancer.
options.D: It is a dangerous medication that should not be used until more research is done.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案是 B。全文的核心在於介紹 daraxonrasib 作為胰臟癌治療的新突破，同時引用專家觀點，強調其初步成效顯著但仍需更多後續研究（如第五、七段所述）。選項 A 過於誇大，文章明確否定了「永久治癒」的說法。選項 C 錯誤，因為目前研究主要針對胰臟癌，其他癌症僅是未來潛在的應用方向。選項 D 錯誤，文章語氣正面，並非將其視為危險藥物。
